templates.pattern: Light passes from medium 1 (refractive index [N1]) through medium 2 into medium 3 (refractive index [N3]). What is the effective refractive index from medium 1 to medium 3?
templates.explanation: Effective refractive index = n3 ÷ n1 = [N3] ÷ [N1] = [RESULT]. The intermediate medium does not affect the overall ratio.

templates.pattern: An optical fibre has a core refractive index of [NC] and cladding refractive index of [NK]. What is the sine of the critical angle at the core-cladding boundary?
templates.explanation: sin C = n_cladding ÷ n_core = [NK] ÷ [NC] = [RESULT]. Light hitting the boundary beyond this critical angle undergoes total internal reflection and stays inside the fibre.

templates.pattern: A thin converging lens of focal length [F] cm has an object placed [U] cm from it. What is the image distance v in cm?
templates.explanation: Thin lens formula: v = uF ÷ (u−F) = [U]×[F] ÷ ([U]−[F]) = [U*F] ÷ [U-F] = [RESULT] cm

templates.pattern: Two thin lenses of focal lengths [F1] cm and [F2] cm are placed in contact. What is the combined focal length in cm?
templates.explanation: For lenses in contact: 1/F = 1/F1 + 1/F2 → F = F1×F2 ÷ (F1+F2) = [F1]×[F2] ÷ ([F1]+[F2]) = [RESULT] cm

templates.pattern: A lens has power [P1] dioptres and a second lens has power [P2] dioptres. They are placed in contact. What is the combined power in dioptres?
templates.explanation: Powers of lenses in contact simply add: P_total = P1 + P2 = [P1] + [P2] = [RESULT] dioptres
